svg.title: Entry lifecycle and fenced fetch
svg.desc: A key moves from absent to a placeholder with an in-flight fetch, then finalize_fetch stores the body only if the state instance, the generation and the tenant and global epochs still match what was recorded at fetch start. Delete, epoch bump, expiry and eviction return the key to absent.
svg.text: Figure 4.3: Entry lifecycle, single-flight fetch and the fences in finalize_fetch
Absent
no KeyState
miss
Placeholder, op in flight
entry = None, key bytes charged
finalize
Resident
entry stamped with epochs; policy.on_insert
begin_fetch_atomic (shard mutex held)
1. Hit? epochs equal and created_at + ttl > now: return Hit, on_hit.
2. Epoch mismatch: drop entry, generation + 1.
3. in_flight has the key: push a oneshot waiter (limit 1,000).
4. Else make room (up to 32 evictions), or CapacityExceeded.
5. Leader: new op_id, record op_gen = generation, stamp
entry epochs = epochs now, insert SharedOp in in_flight.
Origin fetch (spawned task, no lock held)
permit from the origin gate, 5 s response read timeout
finalize_fetch (shard mutex held)
a. detach in_flight if op_id matches; take waiters.
b. state_instance_id equal? else stale_ops_ignored.
c. op_id still in active_op_ids? remove it.
d. Success only: generation == op_gen AND
entry epochs == epochs read now (fence #1).
e. byte budget: evict up to 32, else reject.
f. store; re-read epochs and stamp (G4A-01 site).
Stored
waiters get the body,
entry becomes Resident
Rejected
waiters still get body;
stale_writes_prevented
Ways a Resident entry leaves (each updates bytes)
delete(key): entry None, generation + 1, in_flight detached.
Epoch bump: lazy. The next read sees a mismatch and drops it.
TTL passed: not served as a hit; the sweeper reclaims it later
(kept for stale-while-revalidate / stale-if-error windows).
Eviction: policy picks an unpinned victim when full.
Pinned = key has an active op or an in-flight fetch.
Pinned keys are never evicted.
Why each fence exists
instance id: a state removed and recreated must not accept a finish from the older state.
generation: delete() bumps it, so a fetch that started before a DELETE cannot store its body afterwards.
epochs: tenant or global invalidation bumps an epoch without touching any shard; the entry stamped at fetch start must still match.
Epoch bumps do NOT change the per-key generation, so only the epoch comparison protects against them.
